newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures slip, more spot gold falls seen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures slip, more spot gold falls seen.

text.p: Yen-based gold futures extended early losses to end lower in quiet trade on Monday, while bullion was pushed down by selling by Australian producers in overwhelmingly bearish sentiment, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from three yen to seven yen per gram lower, with benchmark October ending down five yen at 1,339 yen.

In the spot gold market, bullion was quoted at $370.25/55 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $371.25/45 in London on Friday. "Everybody believes spot gold will fall to $368 per ounce," one trader said.
Traders said Australian producers are expected to sell more gold, due partly to fears that an expected further rise in the Australian dollar will batter local gold prices.
The traders said concerns that European central banks will sell their gold reserves will also intensify already bearish market sentiment.
Overseas funds that have built massive short positions recently are likely to wait for further gold falls before covering positions, they said.
In gold futures, local investors retreated to the sidelines as a weaker yen was offset by falls in bullion prices.
Traders said large long positions still held by private investors in the December contracts of gold and platinum were still casting a shadow on the markets.
"The gold and platinum futures could be volatile as private investors are waiting for a chance to liquidate their positions ahead of the spot expiry later this month," the trader said.
Benchmark October platinum was down three yen per gram at 1,362 yen. Benchmark October silver was down 0.8 yen per 10 grams at 174.9 yen. Benchmark October palladium was flat at 422 yen.
